name: brush-chart
title: Brush Chart
description: A long series with an overview strip: drag the window or its handles and the chart above zooms to it.

perf.budget: Two Skia canvases. The visible part is rebuilt on the UI thread while dragging; the overview path is built once per size. Nothing runs at rest.

measurements.notes: Before the window stopped re-rendering React on every drag frame this was 32 ms median with 36% janky frames.

a11y.reducedMotion: Screen reader steps move the window at once instead of springing.
a11y.screenReader: The chart is an image that reads the visible range and its first and last values; the strip is an adjustable range.
a11y.touchTarget: The whole strip is the target, 52 pt tall; handles respond 22 pt either side.

meta.guide:
## Usage

```tsx
import { BrushChart } from '@/components/kinetik/brush-chart';

<BrushChart
  accessibilityLabel="Daily visitors"
  data={visitors}
  labels={dates}
  initialWindow={[0.7, 1]}
  onWindowChange={([from, to]) => load(from, to)}
/>;
```

## When to use

- Long time series where people need both the shape of the whole and the detail of a part: traffic, prices, sensor readings.
- Dashboards where the visible range drives other figures, via `onWindowChange`.

## When not to use

- A handful of points. Use Line Chart or Bar Chart.
- Comparing several series. Use Line Chart with a legend.

## Notes

- Drag inside the window to move it, pull either handle to zoom, or tap outside it to jump there.
- The main chart is rebuilt on the UI thread from the window and rescales to the visible range; the overview is drawn once per size.
- The readout shows the last visible value and the change across the window, and updates when the window settles. The range is an adjustable element: screen readers step it by half a window.
- `onWindowChange` receives the first and last visible point indices when the window settles.

docs: Prefer `npx kinetik-ui add brush-chart`: it installs dependencies with expo install, so versions match your Expo SDK.
